Attribute agreement of a categorical LLM pipeline

Source: R/agreement.R
msa_agreement.Rd

The categorical counterpart of msa_grr(), following the attribute agreement analysis of the AIAG MSA manual: how often does the pipeline give the same answer when asked again (repeatability), the same answer under a different prompt or model (reproducibility), and the correct answer (accuracy against a reference)? Agreement is summarised as percentages of consistent cells and items, as Krippendorff's alpha (which tolerates missing responses and ordinal scales) and, against a reference, as Cohen's kappa with optional ordinal weights.

Usage

msa_agreement(
  runs,
  levels = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  weights = c("unweighted", "linear", "quadratic")
)

Arguments

runs

An msa_runs object with categorical values.

levels

The labels in scale order (needed for ordinal weights and for a clean category list). Default: sorted unique values.

reference

Optional reference classification: a named vector keyed by item_id, a data.frame with columns item_id and reference, or the name of a column in runs.

weights

Weighting of disagreements for the ordinal statistics: "unweighted" (nominal), "linear" or "quadratic".

Value

An object of class msa_agreement, a list with repeatability (per prompt-model cell: share of items whose replicates all agree), reproducibility (share of items consistent across prompts, across models and overall), alpha (Krippendorff's alpha within replicates, across prompts, across models, and overall), and, if a reference is given, accuracy (per prompt-model and overall) and kappa (Cohen's kappa of the modal response and of all responses against the reference).

Examples

lv <- c("B", "LB", "VUS", "LP", "P")
ag <- msa_agreement(acmg_demo, levels = lv, reference = "reference", weights = "linear")
ag
#> Attribute agreement of an LLM measurement system
#>   60 items, 2160 responses (12 missing/unparseable); categories: B < LB < VUS < LP < P; weights: linear
#> 
#> Repeatability: 43.4 % of item-prompt-model cells have identical replicates
#>  prompt_id model_id pct_items_consistent
#>    concise  model-a               40.0 %
#>   criteria  model-a               38.3 %
#>       json  model-a               41.7 %
#>       role  model-a               43.3 %
#>    concise  model-b               45.0 %
#>   criteria  model-b               40.0 %
#>       json  model-b               35.6 %
#>       role  model-b               45.0 %
#>    concise  model-c               48.3 %
#>   criteria  model-c               51.7 %
#>       json  model-c               45.0 %
#>       role  model-c               46.7 %
#> 
#> Reproducibility: items consistent across prompts 16.7 %, across models 15.8 %, overall 8.3 %
#> 
#> Krippendorff's alpha:
#>                               scope alpha
#>  replicates (within prompt & model) 0.876
#>       across prompts (within model) 0.874
#>       across models (within prompt) 0.839
#>                      all conditions 0.839
#> 
#> Accuracy vs reference: 60.8 % of responses correct; 8.3 % of items correct in every call
#>  prompt_id model_id pct_correct
#>    concise  model-a      59.0 %
#>   criteria  model-a      58.2 %
#>       json  model-a      63.3 %
#>       role  model-a      62.0 %
#>    concise  model-b      66.7 %
#>   criteria  model-b      66.1 %
#>       json  model-b      67.4 %
#>       role  model-b      60.5 %
#>    concise  model-c      50.0 %
#>   criteria  model-c      53.3 %
#>       json  model-c      58.9 %
#>       role  model-c      64.8 %
